It's the primary output format for **GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS, NAM**, and similar numerical weather prediction products.\n54\t\n55\tDecoding it means handling multi-section message framing, four grid geometries, parameter tables indexed by discipline/category/number, five data-packing algorithms, and bitmaps for missing-value masking.\n56\t\n57\tThe standard tools (`wgrib2`, `eccodes`) are C programs. If you need decoded GRIB2 values in a Rust project, your options were: shell out, bind through FFI, or give up and parse bytes yourself.\n58\t\n59\t**gribtract is the native Rust alternative.**\n60\t\n61\t## ✨ Features\n62\t\n63\t- 🦀 **Pure Rust core** — no C toolchain or FFI for simple, complex, complex+spatial-differencing, and PNG packing (DRT 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.41); JPEG2000 (5.40) available behind the optional `jpeg2000` feature\n64\t- 🏷️ **Typed output** — every decoded field carries structured metadata: parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n65\t- 🗺️ **Four grid projections** — lat/lon (GDT 3.0), polar stereographic (3.20), Lambert conformal (3.30), Gaussian (3.40)\n66\t- ⚡ **Lazy decode path** — parse headers only, defer grid data; extract single grid points in **O(1)** for DRT=0 fields without decoding the full grid\n67\t- 📈 **Timeseries extractor** — pull per-station forecast series for a list of lat/lon coordinates in one call\n68\t- 🌐 **Byte-range fetching** — `gribtract-fetch` downloads GRIB2 (or slices of it) from NOAA S3, GCS, and NOMADS over HTTP range requests\n69\t- 🐍 **Python bindings** — `gribtract-py` (PyO3) exposes the decoder to Python\n70\t- ✅ **Oracle-gated correctness** — every release is verified against eccodes/wgrib2 over a corpus of real NOAA files; agreement can only ratchet up\n71\t\n72\t## 🌍 Geographic Coverage\n73\t\n74\tgribtract provides comprehensive coverage for CONUS (Continental United States) weather station data extraction, validated against real NOAA HRRR CONUS GRIB2 files.\n75\t\n76\t### Validated Coverage Areas\n77\t\n78\t**CONUS Coverage:** ✅ **100% station coverage confirmed** (56/56 stations tested)\n79\t\n80\tThe HRRR CONUS grid (Lambert Conformal Conic, 3km resolution) covers:\n81\t- **Northern extent:** 48.57°N (International Falls, MN)\n82\t- **Southern extent:** 25.91°N (Brownsville, TX) \n83\t- **Western extent:** 122.60°W (Portland, OR)\n84\t- **Eastern extent:** 71.01°W (Boston, MA)\n85\t\n86\t### Station Coverage by Region\n87\t\n88\t| Region | Stations | Coverage | Notes |\n89\t|--------|----------|----------|-------|\n90\t| East Coast | 5 | 100% | 4 marginal stations near grid edge |\n91\t| Southeast | 8 | 100% | Florida peninsula covered |\n92\t| Midwest | 8 | 100% | Excellent coverage, no edge issues |\n93\t| South Central | 7 | 100% | Well-covered region |\n94\t| Mountain | 4 | 100% | No coverage gaps |\n95\t| West Coast | 8 | 100% | 7 marginal stations near grid edge |\n96\t| Southwest | 4 | 100% | Good coverage |\n97\t| Northern Border | 6 | 100% | Complete border coverage |\n98\t| Southern Border | 5 | 100% | Complete border coverage |\n99\t\n100\t### Geographic Limitations\n101\t\n102\t⚠️ **Edge Proximity:** ~27% of tested stations are within 100 km of grid boundaries, particularly:\n103\t- **West Coast stations:** Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, Los Angeles (near eastern grid edge)\n104\t- **East Coast stations:** Boston, New York, Philadelphia (near western grid edge)\n105\t- **Florida stations:** Miami, Ft. Lauderdale (near southern grid edge)\n106\t\n107\tThis is expected behavior for the HRRR CONUS domain, which is optimized for CONUS coverage with minimal buffer beyond coastlines.\n108\t\n109\t### Grid Specifications\n110\t\n111\t| Parameter | Value |\n112\t|-----------|-------|\n113\t| **Grid Type** | Lambert Conformal Conic (GDT 30) |\n114\t| **Resolution** | 3.0 km × 3.0 km |\n115\t| **Grid Points** | 1,905,141 (1799 × 1059) |\n116\t| **Projection Origin** | 38.5°N, -97.5°W (Central CONUS) |\n117\t| **Coverage Radius** | ~2,000 km from origin |\n118\t\n119\t### Detailed Documentation\n120\t\n121\tFor complete coverage validation results, station lists, and methodology, see:\n122\t- **[CONUS Coverage Validation Summary](docs/conus-coverage-validation-summary.md)** - Comprehensive analysis and findings\n123\t- **[CONUS Coverage Map](docs/conus-coverage-map.txt)** - Detailed ASCII coverage visualization\n124\t- **[Detailed Station Analysis](notes/bf-5jgf0.md)** - Complete 56-station breakdown\n125\t\n126\t## 📦 Crate Layout\n127\t\n128\t```\n129\tgribtract/\n130\t├── crates/\n131\t│   ├── gribtract-core      # 🔩 Section parser, template decoders, unpacking. No I/O.\n132\t│   ├── gribtract           # 📚 High-level API: message iterator, field selection, timeseries\n133\t│   ├── gribtract-cli       # 💻 `gribtract decode|list|dump` command-line tool\n134\t│   ├── gribtract-fetch     # 🌐 HTTP byte-range fetching from S3 / GCS / NOMADS\n135\t│   ├── gribtract-py        # 🐍 Python bindings via PyO3 (excluded from default build)\n136\t│   └── gribtract-testutil  # 🧪 Differential harness: corpus, golden fixtures, diff\n137\t└── xtask                   # 🛠️ Corpus management, reference-decoder runner, bench dashboard\n138\t```\n139\t\n140\t`gribtract-core` is the zero-dependency parsing core. `gribtract` is the crate you depend on for library use. `gribtract-cli` builds the standalone `gribtract` binary.\n141\t\n142\t## 📖 Usage\n143\t\n144\t### Decode all fields from a GRIB2 file\n145\t\n146\t```rust\n147\tuse gribtract::{decode, Field};\n148\t\n149\tlet bytes = std::fs::read(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\")?;\n150\tlet fields: Vec<Field> = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\n151\t\n152\tfor field in &fields {\n153\t    println!(\n154\t        \"param={}/{}/{}  level={}  forecast_offset={}h\",\n155\t        field.parameter.discipline,\n156\t        field.parameter.category,\n157\t        field.parameter.number,\n158\t        field.level.value1(),\n159\t        field.forecast_time.offset_seconds() / 3600,\n160\t    );\n161\t}\n162\t```\n163\t\n164\t### Extract a single grid point — O(1), no full decode\n165\t\n166\t```rust\n167\tuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_point_drt0};\n168\t\n169\tlet fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\n170\tfor lf in &fields {\n171\t    if let Some(body) = &lf.section7_raw {\n172\t        let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(40.64, -73.78)?; // JFK\n173\t        if let Some(value) = decode_point_drt0(body, &lf.packing, idx) {\n174\t            println!(\"value at JFK: {value}\");\n175\t        }\n176\t    }\n177\t}\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\t### Extract a forecast timeseries for a list of stations\n181\t\n182\t```rust\n183\tuse gribtract::timeseries::{extract_timeseries, ParameterRecord, Station, TimeseriesRequest};\n184\t\n185\t// 2m temperature (discipline=0, category=0, number=0), height-above-ground level (type=103)\n186\tlet request = TimeseriesRequest {\n187\t    parameter: ParameterRecord { discipline: 0, category: 0, number: 0 },\n188\t    level_type1: 103,\n189\t    stations: vec![\n190\t        Station { id: \"JFK\".into(), lat: 40.64,  lon: -73.78  },\n191\t        Station { id: \"ORD\".into(), lat: 41.979, lon: -87.905 },\n192\t        Station { id: \"LAX\".into(), lat: 33.943, lon: -118.408 },\n193\t    ],\n194\t};\n195\t\n196\tlet fields = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\n197\tlet ts = extract_timeseries(&fields, &request);\n198\t\n199\tfor (station, rows) in &ts.stations {\n200\t    println!(\"Station: {station}\");\n201\t    for row in rows {\n202\t        println!(\"  forecast hour {}: {:?}\", row.forecast_hour, row.value);\n203\t    }\n204\t}\n205\t```\n206\t\n207\t### Decode a DRT=3 grid (complex + spatial differencing) — extract many stations\n208\t\n209\tDRT=3 requires a full sequential decode; random access isn't possible. The recommended pattern is **decode once, extract many**:\n210\t\n211\t```rust\n212\tuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_all_drt3};\n213\t\n214\tlet lazy_fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\n215\tfor lf in &lazy_fields {\n216\t    if let (Some(body), Some(extra)) = (&lf.section7_raw, &lf.complex_extra) {\n217\t        let n = lf.grid.num_data_points as usize;\n218\t        let grid: Vec<f64> = decode_all_drt3(body, &lf.packing, extra, n)?;\n219\t\n220\t        // Now extract any number of stations by index, O(1) each\n221\t        for (lat, lon) in &station_coords {\n222\t            let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(*lat, *lon)?;\n223\t            println!(\"value: {}\", grid[idx]);\n224\t        }\n225\t    }\n226\t}\n227\t```\n228\t\n229\t### 🐍 Python\n230\t\n231\t```bash\n232\tpip install maturin\n233\tmaturin develop -p gribtract-py\n234\t```\n235\t\n236\t```python\n237\timport gribtract\n238\t\n239\tfields = gribtract.decode(open(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\", \"rb\").read())\n240\tfor f in fields:\n241\t    print(f.parameter, f.level, f.forecast_hour)\n242\t```\n243\t\n244\t## 🔬 The Correctness Oracle\n245\t\n246\tgribtract is built **oracle-first**: correctness is defined as agreement with eccodes/wgrib2 over real files, not as passing hand-written unit tests.\n247\t\n248\t```\n249\tgribtract decode  ─┐\n250\t                   ├─→ compare field-by-field + grid values within derived tolerance\n251\teccodes/wgrib2    ─┘\n252\t```\n253\t\n254\tThe differential harness in `gribtract-testutil` runs both decoders over a corpus of real NOAA GRIB2 files (GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS) and compares:\n255\t\n256\t- **Metadata exactly** — center, parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n257\t- **Grid values within derived tolerance** — computed from the packing template's own scale factors, never an arbitrary epsilon\n258\t\n259\tAny disagreement becomes a permanent regression fixture. The agreement percentage can only increase; there is no mechanism to silently drop a covered template.\n260\t\n261\t```bash\n262\t# Run the differential tests\n263\tcargo test -p gribtract -- differential\n264\t\n265\t# Fetch and verify against the full corpus (requires eccodes installed)\n266\tcargo xtask corpus fetch\n267\tcargo xtask corpus verify\n268\t```\n269\t\n270\t## 📊 Performance Dashboard\n271\t\n272\tA self-contained benchmark dashboard (`dashboard.html`) tracks decode throughput on real NOAA files, fed by `bench-results.json`. Core decoding (DRT 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.41) is 100% Rust — JPEG2000 (DRT 5.40) is the one optional feature that pulls in a C dependency (`openjpeg-sys`).\n\n---\n\n## 🚀 Quickstart\n\n```bash\n# 1. It's the primary output format for **GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS, NAM**, and similar numerical weather prediction products.\n\nDecoding it means handling multi-section message framing, four grid geometries, parameter tables indexed by discipline/category/number, five data-packing algorithms, and bitmaps for missing-value masking.\n\nThe standard tools (`wgrib2`, `eccodes`) are C programs. If you need decoded GRIB2 values in a Rust project, your options were: shell out, bind through FFI, or give up and parse bytes yourself.\n\n**gribtract is the native Rust alternative.**\n\n## ✨ Features\n\n- 🦀 **Pure Rust core** — no C toolchain or FFI for simple, complex, complex+spatial-differencing, and PNG packing (DRT 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.41); JPEG2000 (5.40) available behind the optional `jpeg2000` feature\n- 🏷️ **Typed output** — every decoded field carries structured metadata: parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n- 🗺️ **Four grid projections** — lat/lon (GDT 3.0), polar stereographic (3.20), Lambert conformal (3.30), Gaussian (3.40)\n- ⚡ **Lazy decode path** — parse headers only, defer grid data; extract single grid points in **O(1)** for DRT=0 fields without decoding the full grid\n- 📈 **Timeseries extractor** — pull per-station forecast series for a list of lat/lon coordinates in one call\n- 🌐 **Byte-range fetching** — `gribtract-fetch` downloads GRIB2 (or slices of it) from NOAA S3, GCS, and NOMADS over HTTP range requests\n- 🐍 **Python bindings** — `gribtract-py` (PyO3) exposes the decoder to Python\n- ✅ **Oracle-gated correctness** — every release is verified against eccodes/wgrib2 over a corpus of real NOAA files; agreement can only ratchet up\n\n## 🌍 Geographic Coverage\n\ngribtract provides comprehensive coverage for CONUS (Continental United States) weather station data extraction, validated against real NOAA HRRR CONUS GRIB2 files.\n\n### Validated Coverage Areas\n\n**CONUS Coverage:** ✅ **100% station coverage confirmed** (56/56 stations tested)\n\nThe HRRR CONUS grid (Lambert Conformal Conic, 3km resolution) covers:\n- **Northern extent:** 48.57°N (International Falls, MN)\n- **Southern extent:** 25.91°N (Brownsville, TX) \n- **Western extent:** 122.60°W (Portland, OR)\n- **Eastern extent:** 71.01°W (Boston, MA)\n\n### Station Coverage by Region\n\n| Region | Stations | Coverage | Notes |\n|--------|----------|----------|-------|\n| East Coast | 5 | 100% | 4 marginal stations near grid edge |\n| Southeast | 8 | 100% | Florida peninsula covered |\n| Midwest | 8 | 100% | Excellent coverage, no edge issues |\n| South Central | 7 | 100% | Well-covered region |\n| Mountain | 4 | 100% | No coverage gaps |\n| West Coast | 8 | 100% | 7 marginal stations near grid edge |\n| Southwest | 4 | 100% | Good coverage |\n| Northern Border | 6 | 100% | Complete border coverage |\n| Southern Border | 5 | 100% | Complete border coverage |\n\n### Geographic Limitations\n\n⚠️ **Edge Proximity:** ~27% of tested stations are within 100 km of grid boundaries, particularly:\n- **West Coast stations:** Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, Los Angeles (near eastern grid edge)\n- **East Coast stations:** Boston, New York, Philadelphia (near western grid edge)\n- **Florida stations:** Miami, Ft. No I/O.\n│   ├── gribtract           # 📚 High-level API: message iterator, field selection, timeseries\n│   ├── gribtract-cli       # 💻 `gribtract decode|list|dump` command-line tool\n│   ├── gribtract-fetch     # 🌐 HTTP byte-range fetching from S3 / GCS / NOMADS\n│   ├── gribtract-py        # 🐍 Python bindings via PyO3 (excluded from default build)\n│   └── gribtract-testutil  # 🧪 Differential harness: corpus, golden fixtures, diff\n└── xtask                   # 🛠️ Corpus management, reference-decoder runner, bench dashboard\n```\n\n`gribtract-core` is the zero-dependency parsing core. `gribtract` is the crate you depend on for library use. `gribtract-cli` builds the standalone `gribtract` binary.\n\n## 📖 Usage\n\n### Decode all fields from a GRIB2 file\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::{decode, Field};\n\nlet bytes = std::fs::read(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\")?;\nlet fields: Vec<Field> = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\n\nfor field in &fields {\n    println!(\n        \"param={}/{}/{}  level={}  forecast_offset={}h\",\n        field.parameter.discipline,\n        field.parameter.category,\n        field.parameter.number,\n        field.level.value1(),\n        field.forecast_time.offset_seconds() / 3600,\n    );\n}\n```\n\n### Extract a single grid point — O(1), no full decode\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_point_drt0};\n\nlet fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\nfor lf in &fields {\n    if let Some(body) = &lf.section7_raw {\n        let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(40.64, -73.78)?; // JFK\n        if let Some(value) = decode_point_drt0(body, &lf.packing, idx) {\n            println!(\"value at JFK: {value}\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Extract a forecast timeseries for a list of stations\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::timeseries::{extract_timeseries, ParameterRecord, Station, TimeseriesRequest};\n\n// 2m temperature (discipline=0, category=0, number=0), height-above-ground level (type=103)\nlet request = TimeseriesRequest {\n    parameter: ParameterRecord { discipline: 0, category: 0, number: 0 },\n    level_type1: 103,\n    stations: vec![\n        Station { id: \"JFK\".into(), lat: 40.64,  lon: -73.78  },\n        Station { id: \"ORD\".into(), lat: 41.979, lon: -87.905 },\n        Station { id: \"LAX\".into(), lat: 33.943, lon: -118.408 },\n    ],\n};\n\nlet fields = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\nlet ts = extract_timeseries(&fields, &request);\n\nfor (station, rows) in &ts.stations {\n    println!(\"Station: {station}\");\n    for row in rows {\n        println!(\"  forecast hour {}: {:?}\", row.forecast_hour, row.value);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Decode a DRT=3 grid (complex + spatial differencing) — extract many stations\n\nDRT=3 requires a full sequential decode; random access isn't possible. The recommended pattern is **decode once, extract many**:\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_all_drt3};\n\nlet lazy_fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\nfor lf in &lazy_fields {\n    if let (Some(body), Some(extra)) = (&lf.section7_raw, &lf.complex_extra) {\n        let n = lf.grid.num_data_points as usize;\n        let grid: Vec<f64> = decode_all_drt3(body, &lf.packing, extra, n)?;\n\n        // Now extract any number of stations by index, O(1) each\n        for (lat, lon) in &station_coords {\n            let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(*lat, *lon)?;\n            println!(\"value: {}\", grid[idx]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### 🐍 Python\n\n```bash\npip install maturin\nmaturin develop -p gribtract-py\n```\n\n```python\nimport gribtract\n\nfields = gribtract.decode(open(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\", \"rb\").read())\nfor f in fields:\n    print(f.parameter, f.level, f.forecast_hour)\n```\n\n## 🔬 The Correctness Oracle\n\ngribtract is built **oracle-first**: correctness is defined as agreement with eccodes/wgrib2 over real files, not as passing hand-written unit tests.\n\n```\ngribtract decode  ─┐\n                   ├─→ compare field-by-field + grid values within derived tolerance\neccodes/wgrib2    ─┘\n```\n\nThe differential harness in `gribtract-testutil` runs both decoders over a corpus of real NOAA GRIB2 files (GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS) and compares:\n\n- **Metadata exactly** — center, parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n- **Grid values within derived tolerance** — computed from the packing template's own scale factors, never an arbitrary epsilon\n\nAny disagreement becomes a permanent regression fixture. The agreement percentage can only increase; there is no mechanism to silently drop a covered template.\n\n```bash\n# Run the differential tests\ncargo test -p gribtract -- differential\n\n# Fetch and verify against the full corpus (requires eccodes installed)\ncargo xtask corpus fetch\ncargo xtask corpus verify\n```\n\n## 📊 Performance Dashboard\n\nA self-contained benchmark dashboard (`dashboard.html`) tracks decode throughput on real NOAA files, fed by `bench-results.json`. Definition Template (GDT) 3.30 (Lambert-conformal conic) and Data Representation Template (DRT) 5.3 (complex packing).\n\n## Models Using Lambert Conformal Conic Projection (GDT 3.30)\n\n### 1. HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh)\n\n**Characteristics:**\n- **Resolution:** 3km\n- **Domain:** CONUS and Alaska sectors\n- **Projection:** Lambert Conformal Conic (GDT 3.30)\n- **Update frequency:** Hourly (every hour, 00z-23z)\n- **Archive start:** September 30, 2014 (University of Utah archive)\n\n**File Naming Convention:**\n```\nhrrr.tCCz.wrfsfcfFF.grib2\nhrrr.tCCz.wrfprsfFF.grib2\nhrrr.tCCz.wrfnatfFF.grib2\n```\nWhere:\n- `CC` = cycle runtime (00-23)\n- `FF` = forecast hour (00-48)\n\n**Run Schedule:**\n- **Standard cycles:** All hours (00z-23z), forecast out to FH18\n- **Extended cycles:** 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z run out to FH48\n- **Sub-hourly data:** Available for FH01-FH18 (15, 30, 45 min before the hour)\n\n**Typical File Size:** ~120 MB per GRIB2 file\n\n**Archive URLs:**\n- NOAA NCEP: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/hrrr/\n- University of Utah CHPC Archive: https://mesowest.utah.edu/html/hrrr/\n- AWS Open Data Registry: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-hrrr-pds/\n- NOMADS: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/gribfilter.php?ds=hrrr_2d\n\n**Access Methods:**\n- FTP/HTTPS from NCEP servers\n- AWS S3 (noaa-hrrr-pds bucket)\n- NOMADS with subsetting capabilities\n- University of Utah download tool with metadata (.idx) files\n\n### 2. NAM (North American Mesoscale) - Regional Nests\n\n**Characteristics:**\n- **Resolution:** Varies by domain (1.33km - 6km for regional nests)\n- **Domains:** \n  - CONUS Nest (5km, Grid 227)\n  - Alaska Nest (6km, Grid 198)\n  - Hawaii Nest (3km, Grid 196)\n  - Puerto Rico Nest (3km, Grid 194)\n  - Fire Weather Nest (1.33km CONUS / 1.5km Alaska)\n- **Projection:** Lambert Conformal Conic for regional nests\n- **Update frequency:** 4x daily (00z, 06z, 12z, 18z)\n\n**File Naming Convention:**\n```\nnam.tCCz.conusnest.hiresffh.tm00.grib2\nnam.tCCz.alaskanest.hiresffh.tm00.grib2\nnam.tCCz.hawaiinest.hiresffh.tm00.grib2\nnam.tCCz.priconest.hiresffh.tm00.grib2\nnam.tCCz.firewxnest.hiresffh.tm00.grib2\n```\nWhere:\n- `CC` = cycle runtime (00, 06, 12, 18)\n- `ffh` = forecast hour (00-60)\n\n**Run Schedule:**\n- **Cycle times:** 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z\n- **Forecast hours:** FH00-FH60 for most nests (FH00-FH36 for Fire Weather)\n\n**Archive URLs:**\n- NOAA NCEP: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/nam/\n- NOMADS: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/\n- UCAR GDEX: https://gdex.ucar.edu/datasets/d609000/\n- READY Archives: https://www.ready.noaa.gov/archives.php\n\n**Access Methods:**\n- FTP/HTTPS from NCEP servers\n- NOMADS with GRIB2 subsetting\n- AWS S3 commands via READY\n\n### 3. RAP (Rapid Refresh)\n\n**Characteristics:**\n- **Resolution:** 13km (CONUS Lambert Conformal)\n- **Domain:** CONUS on Lambert Conformal projection\n- **Projection:** Lambert Conformal Conic (GDT 3.30)\n- **Update frequency:** Hourly (every hour, 00z-23z)\n\n**File Naming Convention:**\n```\nrap.tCCz.awp130pgrbfxx.grib2  (13km pressure levels)\nrap.tCCz.awp252pgrbfxx.grib2  (20km pressure levels)\nrap.tCCz.awp236pgrbfxx.grib2  (40km pressure levels)\n```\nWhere:\n- `CC` = cycle runtime (00-23)\n- `xx` = forecast hour\n\n**Run Schedule:**\n- **Standard cycles:** All hours, forecast out to FH21\n- **Extended cycles:** 03z, 09z, 15z, 21z run out to FH51\n\n**Archive URLs:**\n- NOAA NCEP: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/rap/\n- AWS Open Data Registry: https://registry.opendata.aws/collab/noaa/\n\n**Access Methods:**\n- FTP/HTTPS from NCEP servers\n- AWS S3 (noaa-rap-pds bucket)\n\n## GRIB2 Encoding Specifications\n\n### Grid Definition Template 3.30: Lambert Conformal Conic\n\n**Documentation:**\n- NOAA NCO: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/docs/grib2/grib2_doc/grib2_temp3-30.shtml\n- NCEP Table 3.1: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/docs/grib2/grib2_doc/grib2_table3-1.shtml\n\n**Key Parameters:**\n- Grid lengths in units of 10^-3 m at specified latitude (LaD)\n- If Latin1 = Latin2, projection is on a tangent cone\n- LoV is the longitude of the meridian parallel to the y-axis (orientation)\n\n### Data Representation Template 5.3: Complex Packing with Spatial Differencing\n\n**Documentation:**\n- NOAA NCO: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/docs/grib2/grib2_doc/grib2_temp5-3.shtml\n- ECMWF Code Table 5.0: https://codes.ecmwf.int/grib/format/grib2/ctables/5/0/\n\n**Description:**\n- \"Grid point data - 00, 03, 06, ..., 87 (every 3 hours)\n167\t- **Forecast Range:** 0-87 hours (3.6 days)\n168\t- **Members:** 21 members\n169\t- **Status:** Proposed for termination (July 2025), may be replaced by GEFS\n170\t\n171\t---\n172\t\n173\t## 3. HREF (High Resolution Ensemble Forecast)\n174\t\n175\t### Archive Infrastructure\n176\t\n177\t**Archive Platform:** NOMADS  \n178\t**Access:** HTTP (directory browsing)  \n179\t**Status:** Being discontinued (replaced by REFS)\n180\t\n181\t### URL Pattern\n182\t\n183\t**NOMADS Pattern:**\n184\t```\n185\thttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/href/prod/href.YYYYMMDD/HH/[filename]\n186\t```\n187\t\n188\t**Components:**\n189\t- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n190\t- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n191\t- **[filename]** = Ensemble member file\n192\t\n193\t### File Naming Conventions\n194\t\n195\t**HREF Members:**\n196\tHREF is a convection-allowing ensemble (~3km resolution) with multiple members:\n197\t- **arw** = Advanced Research WRF\n198\t- **nmm** = Non-hydrostatic Mesoscale Model\n199\t- **nssl** = NSSL configuration\n200\t- Other configurations\n201\t\n202\t**File Pattern:**\n203\t```\n204\thref_[member]_tCCz_fFF_GRIB2\n205\t```\n206\t\n207\t### Example URLs\n208\t\n209\t```\n210\t# HREF directory listing, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle\n211\thttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/href/prod/href.20260723/00/\n212\t\n213\t# ARW member, 00z cycle, analysis\n214\thref_arw_t00z_f00.grib2\n215\t\n216\t# NSSL member, 12z cycle, 6-hour forecast\n217\thref_nssl_t12z_f06.grib2\n218\t```\n219\t\n220\t### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n221\t\n222\t- **Cycle Frequency:** 2x daily (00z, 12z)\n223\t- **Forecast Range:** Typically 0-30 hours\n224\t- **Resolution:** ~3km (convection-allowing)\n225\t- **Status:** Products being discontinued, see SCN26-048\n226\t\n227\t---\n228\t\n229\t## 4. NBM (National Blend of Models)\n230\t\n231\t### Archive Infrastructure\n232\t\n233\t**Archive Platform:** AWS Open Data Registry  \n234\t**Bucket:** `noaa-nbm-grib2-pds`  \n235\t**Region:** us-east-1  \n236\t**Access:** Public HTTP/S3 (no authentication required)\n237\t\n238\t### URL Pattern\n239\t\n240\t**AWS S3 Pattern:**\n241\t```\n242\thttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/core/[filename]\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\t**Components:**\n246\t- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n247\t- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n248\t- **core** = CONUS core grid product directory\n249\t\n250\t### File Naming Conventions\n251\t\n252\t**Core Files:**\n253\t```\n254\tblend.tCCz.core.fFFF.RR.grib2\n255\t```\n256\t\n257\t**QMD Files:**\n258\t```\n259\tblend.tCCz.qmd.fFFF.RR.grib2\n260\t```\n261\t\n262\t**Where:**\n263\t- `CC` = Cycle hour (00, 06, 12, 18)\n264\t- `FFF` = Three-digit forecast hour (001, 002, ..., 084)\n265\t- `RR` = Region code (co = CONUS, other regions for other products)\n266\t- `qmd` = QMD (quasi-model) output\n267\t\n268\t### Example URLs\n269\t\n270\t```\n271\t# Core blend, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle, 1-hour forecast\n272\thttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/00/core/blend.t00z.core.f001.co.grib2\n273\t\n274\t# Core blend, 12-hour forecast\n275\thttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/00/core/blend.t00z.core.f012.co.grib2\n276\t\n277\t# QMD product, 6z cycle, 24-hour forecast\n278\thttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/06/core/blend.t06z.qmd.f024.co.grib2\n279\t\n280\t# Maximum forecast range (84 hours)\n281\thttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/12/core/blend.t12z.core.f084.co.grib2\n282\t```\n283\t\n284\t### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n285\t\n286\t- **Cycle Frequency:** 4x daily (00z, 06z, 12z, 18z)\n287\t- **Forecast Hours:** 001-084 (hourly forecasts)\n288\t- **Forecast Range:** 0-84 hours (3.5 days)\n289\t- **Update Frequency:** Hourly (updated every hour)\n290\t\n291\t### Important Notes\n292\t\n293\t**NBM is a Deterministic Product:**  \n294\tUnlike GEFS, SREF, or HREF, NBM produces deterministic (single) forecasts that blend inputs from multiple ensemble systems including:\n295\t- GEFS (Global Ensemble Forecast System)\n296\t- HREF (High Resolution Ensemble Forecast) - before discontinuation\n297\t- SREF (Short Range Ensemble Forecast)\n298\t- Canadian ensemble forecasts\n299\t\n300\tNBM does not produce individual ensemble member files; instead, it provides calibrated probabilistic guidance based on ensemble inputs.\n301\t\n302\t---\n303\t\n304\t## 5. NAEFS (North American Ensemble Forecast System)\n305\t\n306\t### Archive Infrastructure\n307\t\n308\t**Archive Platform:** MSC Datamart (Meteorological Service of Canada)  \n309\t**Access:** HTTP via weather.gc.ca\n310\t\n311\t### URL Pattern\n312\t\n313\t**MSC Datamart Pattern:**\n314\t```\n315\thttps://[server].weather.gc.ca/ensemble/naefs/[product]/[path]\n316\t```\n317\t\n318\t**Components:**\n319\t- NAEFS is a joint MSC/NOAA project combining ensembles from both agencies\n320\t- Data accessible through MSC's Datamart server\n321\t- Specific file naming patterns vary by product type\n322\t\n323\t### Product Types\n324\t\n325\t- Temperature Anomaly Forecast (Day 8-14)\n326\t- EPSgrams (ensemble time series)\n327\t- Standard Deviation/Mean Charts\n328\t- Probability maps\n329\t\n330\t### Documentation\n331\t\n332\t**Primary Documentation:**\n333\t- [MSC Open Data Documentation](https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/msc-data/nwp_naefs/readme_naefs_en/)\n334\t- [CPC NAEFS Products](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/short_range/NAEFS/)\n335\t\n336\t**Note:** Detailed URL patterns for individual ensemble member files are not as well-documented as GEFS or SREF.\n337\t\n338\t---\n339\t\n340\t## GEFS Reforecast Data (Historical Archive)\n341\t\n342\t### Archive Infrastructure\n343\t\n344\t**Bucket:** `noaa-gefs-retrospective.s3.amazonaws.com`  \n345\t**Access:** Public S3 (no authentication required)\n346\t\n347\t### Description\n348\t\n349\tGEFSv12 reforecast data spanning 2000-2019 is available on AWS. NOAA Ensemble Product URL Patterns\n\n## Summary\n\nThis document provides URL patterns and directory structures for accessing NOAA ensemble/statistical products in public archives. Ensemble systems produce multiple forecasts (members) to quantify forecast uncertainty.\n\n**Date:** 2026-07-23  \n**Purpose:** Reference for constructing URLs to access NOAA ensemble model data archives\n\n---\n\n## Overview of NOAA Ensemble Systems\n\n| System | Type | Members | Coverage | Access Method |\n|--------|------|---------|----------|----------------|\n| **GEFS** | Global Medium-Range | 31 (1 control + 30 perturbed) | Global | AWS S3 |\n| **SREF** | Regional Short-Range | 21 | North America | NOMADS |\n| **HREF** | High-Resolution Convective | ~7 | CONUS | NOMADS (discontinued) |\n| **NBM** | Statistical Blend | Deterministic | CONUS | AWS S3 |\n| **NAEFS** | International Joint | 40 | North America | MSC Datamart |\n\n---\n\n## 1. GEFS (Global Ensemble Forecast System)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Archive Platform:** AWS Open Data Registry  \n**Bucket:** `noaa-gefs-pds`  \n**Region:** us-east-1  \n**Access:** Public HTTP/S3 (no authentication required)\n\n### URL Pattern\n\n**AWS S3 Pattern:**\n```\nhttps://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.YYYYMMDD/HH/[product]/[filename]\n```\n\n**Components:**\n- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n- **[product]** = `pgrb2a` (83 common parameters) or `pgrb2b` (425 less common)\n- **[filename]** = Ensemble member file\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**Control Member (c00):**\n```\ngec00.tXXz.pgrb2aanl      # Analysis\ngec00.tXXz.pgrb2afVV      # Forecast\n```\n\n**Perturbation Members (p01-p30):**\n```\ngepWW.tXXz.pgrb2aanl      # Analysis\ngepWW.tXXz.pgrb2afVV      # Forecast\n```\n\n**Where:**\n- `XX` = Cycle hour from path (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n- `WW` = Ensemble member number (01-20 for some configs, 01-30 for others)\n- `VV` = Forecast hour (00, 06, 12, ..., 384)\n\n### Example URLs\n\n```\n# Control member analysis, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle\nhttps://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.20260723/00/pgrb2a/gec00.t00z.pgrb2aanl\n\n# Perturbation member 05, 12-hour forecast, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle\nhttps://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.20260723/00/pgrb2a/gep05.t00z.pgrb2af012.grib2\n\n# Control member, 48-hour forecast, pgrb2b product\nhttps://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.20260723/12/pgrb2b/gec00.t12z.pgrb2af048.grib2\n\n# Member 30, max range forecast (384 hours)\nhttps://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.20260723/18/pgrb2a/gep30.t18z.pgrb2af384.grib2\n```\n\n### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n\n- **Cycle Frequency:** 4x daily (00z, 06z, 12z, 18z)\n- **Forecast Hours:** 00, 06, 12, 18, ..., 384 (every 6 hours)\n- **Forecast Range:** 0-16 days\n- **Members:** 31 members (control + 30 perturbations)\n\n### Directory Structure Example\n\n```\ngefs.20260723/\n├── 00/\n│   ├── pgrb2a/\n│   │   ├── gec00.t00z.pgrb2aanl\n│   │   ├── gec00.t00z.pgrb2af000.grib2\n│   │   ├── gep01.t00z.pgrb2aanl\n│   │   ├── gep01.t00z.pgrb2af000.grib2\n│   │   ├── gep02.t00z.pgrb2aanl\n│   │   └── ...\n│   └── pgrb2b/\n│       └── ...\n├── 06/\n├── 12/\n└── 18/\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. SREF (Short Range Ensemble Forecast)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Archive Platform:** NOMADS (NOAA Operational Model Archive and Distribution System)  \n**Access:** HTTP (directory browsing)  \n**Retention:** ~30 days operational, longer via NCEI archive\n\n### URL Pattern\n\n**NOMADS Pattern:**\n```\nhttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/sref/prod/sref.YYYYMMDD/HH/[filename]\n```\n\n**Components:**\n- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (03, 09, 15, or 21)\n- **[filename]** = Ensemble member file\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**File Pattern:**\n```\npgrb/sref_[model].tCCz.pgrb212.PP...\n```\n\n**Where:**\n- `model` = Model type (nmm, nmb, em)\n- `CC` = Cycle hour (03, 09, 15, 21)\n- `PP` = Forecast hour (00, 03, 06, ..., 87)\n\n**Ensemble Member Identification:**\nSREF uses 21 members from 4 regional models:\n- **ctl** = Control member (ensemble mean)\n- **g01-g20** = Individual ensemble members\n\n### Example URLs\n\n```\n# SREF directory listing, July 23, 2026, 03z cycle\nhttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/sref/prod/sref.20260723/03/\n\n# Individual member files (example patterns):\n# NMM model, 03z cycle, analysis\npgrb/sref_nmm.t03z.pgrb212.00\n\n# NMB model, 03z cycle, 12-hour forecast\npgrb/sref_nmb.t03z.pgrb212.12\n\n# EM model, 09z cycle, 36-hour forecast\npgrb/sref_em.t09z.pgrb212.36\n```\n\n### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n\n- **Cycle Frequency:** 4x daily (03z, 09z, 15z, 21z)\n- **Forecast Hours:** 00, 03, 06, ..., 87 (every 3 hours)\n- **Forecast Range:** 0-87 hours (3.6 days)\n- **Members:** 21 members\n- **Status:** Proposed for termination (July 2025), may be replaced by GEFS\n\n---\n\n## 3. HREF (High Resolution Ensemble Forecast)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Archive Platform:** NOMADS  \n**Access:** HTTP (directory browsing)  \n**Status:** Being discontinued (replaced by REFS)\n\n### URL Pattern\n\n**NOMADS Pattern:**\n```\nhttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/href/prod/href.YYYYMMDD/HH/[filename]\n```\n\n**Components:**\n- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n- **[filename]** = Ensemble member file\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**HREF Members:**\nHREF is a convection-allowing ensemble (~3km resolution) with multiple members:\n- **arw** = Advanced Research WRF\n- **nmm** = Non-hydrostatic Mesoscale Model\n- **nssl** = NSSL configuration\n- Other configurations\n\n**File Pattern:**\n```\nhref_[member]_tCCz_fFF_GRIB2\n```\n\n### Example URLs\n\n```\n# HREF directory listing, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle\nhttps://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/href/prod/href.20260723/00/\n\n# ARW member, 00z cycle, analysis\nhref_arw_t00z_f00.grib2\n\n# NSSL member, 12z cycle, 6-hour forecast\nhref_nssl_t12z_f06.grib2\n```\n\n### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n\n- **Cycle Frequency:** 2x daily (00z, 12z)\n- **Forecast Range:** Typically 0-30 hours\n- **Resolution:** ~3km (convection-allowing)\n- **Status:** Products being discontinued, see SCN26-048\n\n---\n\n## 4. NBM (National Blend of Models)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Archive Platform:** AWS Open Data Registry  \n**Bucket:** `noaa-nbm-grib2-pds`  \n**Region:** us-east-1  \n**Access:** Public HTTP/S3 (no authentication required)\n\n### URL Pattern\n\n**AWS S3 Pattern:**\n```\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/core/[filename]\n```\n\n**Components:**\n- **YYYYMMDD** = Model run date (e.g., `20260723`)\n- **HH** = Cycle hour directory (00, 06, 12, or 18)\n- **core** = CONUS core grid product directory\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**Core Files:**\n```\nblend.tCCz.core.fFFF.RR.grib2\n```\n\n**QMD Files:**\n```\nblend.tCCz.qmd.fFFF.RR.grib2\n```\n\n**Where:**\n- `CC` = Cycle hour (00, 06, 12, 18)\n- `FFF` = Three-digit forecast hour (001, 002, ..., 084)\n- `RR` = Region code (co = CONUS, other regions for other products)\n- `qmd` = QMD (quasi-model) output\n\n### Example URLs\n\n```\n# Core blend, July 23, 2026, 00z cycle, 1-hour forecast\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/00/core/blend.t00z.core.f001.co.grib2\n\n# Core blend, 12-hour forecast\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/00/core/blend.t00z.core.f012.co.grib2\n\n# QMD product, 6z cycle, 24-hour forecast\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/06/core/blend.t06z.qmd.f024.co.grib2\n\n# Maximum forecast range (84 hours)\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/blend.20260723/12/core/blend.t12z.core.f084.co.grib2\n```\n\n### Cycle Schedule and Forecast Range\n\n- **Cycle Frequency:** 4x daily (00z, 06z, 12z, 18z)\n- **Forecast Hours:** 001-084 (hourly forecasts)\n- **Forecast Range:** 0-84 hours (3.5 days)\n- **Update Frequency:** Hourly (updated every hour)\n\n### Important Notes\n\n**NBM is a Deterministic Product:**  \nUnlike GEFS, SREF, or HREF, NBM produces deterministic (single) forecasts that blend inputs from multiple ensemble systems including:\n- GEFS (Global Ensemble Forecast System)\n- HREF (High Resolution Ensemble Forecast) - before discontinuation\n- SREF (Short Range Ensemble Forecast)\n- Canadian ensemble forecasts\n\nNBM does not produce individual ensemble member files; instead, it provides calibrated probabilistic guidance based on ensemble inputs.\n\n---\n\n## 5. NAEFS (North American Ensemble Forecast System)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Archive Platform:** MSC Datamart (Meteorological Service of Canada)  \n**Access:** HTTP via weather.gc.ca\n\n### URL Pattern\n\n**MSC Datamart Pattern:**\n```\nhttps://[server].weather.gc.ca/ensemble/naefs/[product]/[path]\n```\n\n**Components:**\n- NAEFS is a joint MSC/NOAA project combining ensembles from both agencies\n- Data accessible through MSC's Datamart server\n- Specific file naming patterns vary by product type\n\n### Product Types\n\n- Temperature Anomaly Forecast (Day 8-14)\n- EPSgrams (ensemble time series)\n- Standard Deviation/Mean Charts\n- Probability maps\n\n### Documentation\n\n**Primary Documentation:**\n- [MSC Open Data Documentation](https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/msc-data/nwp_naefs/readme_naefs_en/)\n- [CPC NAEFS Products](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/short_range/NAEFS/)\n\n**Note:** Detailed URL patterns for individual ensemble member files are not as well-documented as GEFS or SREF.\n\n---\n\n## GEFS Reforecast Data (Historical Archive)\n\n### Archive Infrastructure\n\n**Bucket:** `noaa-gefs-retrospective.s3.amazonaws.com`  \n**Access:** Public S3 (no authentication required)\n\n### Description\n\nGEFSv12 reforecast data spanning 2000-2019 is available on AWS. This is a research-quality dataset for model evaluation and calibration.\n\n### Access\n\n**S3 Bucket:**\n```\ns3://noaa-gefs-retrospective/\n```\n\n**Documentation:**\n- Description: `https://noaa-gefs-retrospective.s3.amazonaws.com/Description_of_reforecast_data.pdf`\n- Access via NOAA's PSL Reforecast V2 Project\n\n**Note:** Specific file naming conventions for reforecast data are documented in the PDF description available at the bucket root.\n\n---\n\n## Comparison Table: Ensemble System Characteristics\n\n| System | Access | Cycle Times | Members | Forecast Range | File Extension | URL Structure |\n|--------|--------|-------------|---------|----------------|----------------|----------------|\n| **GEFS** | AWS S3 | 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z | 31 | 0-384h (16d) | .grib2 | `/gefs.YYYYMMDD/HH/pgrb2[a|b]/` |\n| **SREF** | NOMADS | 03z, 09z, 15z, 21z | 21 | 0-87h | varies | `/sref.YYYYMMDD/HH/` |\n| **HREF** | NOMADS | 00z, 12z | ~7 | 0-30h | .grib2 | `/href.YYYYMMDD/HH/` |\n| **NBM** | AWS S3 | 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z | 1 (blend) | 0-84h | .grib2 | `/blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/core/` |\n| **NAEFS** | MSC | Varies | 40 | Varies | Varies | `/ensemble/naefs/` |\n\n---\n\n## Ensemble Member Identification Patterns\n\n| System | Control Member | Perturbed Members | Naming Pattern |\n|--------|---------------|-------------------|----------------|\n| **GEFS** | `gec00` | `gep01`-`gep30` | Prefix + 2-digit number |\n| **SREF** | `ctl` | `g01`-`g20` | Member-specific codes |\n| **HREF** | Varies by model | `arw`, `nmm`, `nssl`, etc. | Model/configuration names |\n| **NBM** | N/A (deterministic) | N/A | N/A (blended product) |\n\n---\n\n## Access Patterns and Rate Limits\n\n### AWS S3 Access (GEFS, NBM)\n\n- **Authentication:** None required (public open data)\n- **Rate Limits:** None observed for typical usage\n- **Range Requests:** Supported (Accept-Ranges: bytes)\n- **CDN:** CloudFront for global distribution\n\n### NOMADS Access (SREF, HREF)\n\n- **Authentication:** None required (public HTTP)\n- **Retention:** ~30 days for operational access\n- **Long-term Archive:** NCEI (National Centers for Environmental Information)\n- **Directory Browsing:** Supported\n\n### Best Practices\n\n1. **For recent cycles (< 30 days):** Use NOMADS or AWS S3\n2. **For historical research:** Use NCEI archive or GEFS reforecast data\n3. **For high-volume access:** Use AWS S3 (no rate limits, better performance)\n4. **For browsing:** Use NOMADS web interface or S3 directory listing\n\n---\n\n## Constructing Ensemble URLs:
